_README: GENERATED by tools/spoils-to-changes.py from Reputation-Matrix2/data/inventory.json — re-run the tool, do not edit.
Items the archive's registry says a party character holds and the exported sheet does not carry.
tools/sheets-suite.py regenerates and applies this on every pass; by hand:
Items are matched by id (flags.waluipedia.inventoryItem), so re-applying is a no-op.
`filed` remembers when each item first came through; `declined` lists items the table removed after seeing
them (delete a row to offer it again). Nothing here touches XP — tools/promote-player-sheets.py pins that to the ledger.

A heavy gold ring designed to capture souls, engraved inside the band with the initials OC. Recovered from the false Lady Aurelian — the Feyward manor’s overgrowth wearing its owner’s face — who cheerfully admitted she struck the real Aurelian in the stomach mid-flight and trapped her in the ring. Currently in Hjumpik’s custody, in the same pocket as Morel’s key, which says something unkind about Hjumpik’s pocket.

  • Captures souls. One reported occupant: the actual Lady of the manor.
  • Band engraved ‘OC’ — the same initials carved into Corvinarus bedframes.
  • Chain of custody this evening: her → Waluigi → her → Waluigi → Hjumpik.
  • Warm as a wrist, which Waluigi finds rude.

Obtained: Blown off the plant lady’s finger by an indoor Bob-omb, grabbed mid-skid by Waluigi, and deposited with the Anvil for absolutely non-negotiable custody.

On the record: party custody — not for sale, appraisal, smashing, or wearing.

Do not smash it, do not sell it, do not let Wario appraise it, and under no circumstances — including formal occasions — does anyone WEAR the soul jar. — W.

description.value:
A signet ring found in the grass on a table in Lady Aurelian’s dark bedroom and recognised by Hjumpik on sight. It can create and destroy connections between the fractured manors: it can speed the ritual of opening the portal, or sever the link entirely. In Hjumpik’s pocket since ~19 Harvestide, 1040 BF (Feyward time).

  • Creates or destroys connections between the manors — a key that can lock and unlock doors, install new ones and take old ones off their frames.
  • Can accelerate the portal-opening ritual, or sever the connection outright.
  • The Book of Revised History, found the same hour, warns the manors must not be combined while a star shard is in play; the ring can honour that warning or ignore it.
  • Not the OC Soul Ring — that one came off the false Lady’s finger four nights later and is a different object.

Obtained: Hjumpik bumped into a table in the dark, squished something that smelled strong, reached into the grass and found the ring under it.

On the record: in Hjumpik’s pocket — merge or sever, undecided.

The ring does not have an opinion about which function is correct. The question is not what the ring can do. The question is who gets to decide what the ring does. — W.

Waluipedia inventory raventree_signet_ring, held by Hjumpik Deldkur — filed from feyward_dark_rooms_and_balcony_planning. Mechanics as the table rules them; the archive records custody.

waluipedia.note: in Hjumpik’s pocket — merge or sever, undecided

description.value:
A book Hjumpik picked out of the vegetation by the couch in Aurelian’s rooms and pocketed like a receipt from a shop. It records Raventree Manor in the 980s BF as a thriving academic centre where Toads, orcs and lightning professors exchanged ideas freely, a proto-Liberated Toads movement there ‘enlightened’ by the Iron Legion and then the Mages Guild, and a warning that the manors must not be combined while a star shard is in play.

  • Raventree in the 980s BF was a school, not a horror: Toads, orcs and lightning professors in free exchange.
  • A proto-Liberated Toads movement at Raventree was ‘enlightened’ — suppressed — by the Iron Legion and then the Mages Guild, sixty years before Order 120.
  • The manors must NOT be combined while a star shard is in play; the Oracle’s plan requires exactly that.
  • Hjumpik’s level of engagement on reading it: background lore. Waluigi’s: among the most important intelligence of the Feyward campaign.

Obtained: Resting on or near the couch, partly buried in leaves, not destroyed; Hjumpik identified it, examined it, handed it to Waluigi to read, and put it in his pocket.

On the record: pocketed like a receipt; read in full by Waluigi.

My colleagues have a persistent, infuriating habit of finding historically critical documents and treating them like grocery lists. — W.

Waluipedia inventory book_of_revised_history, held by Hjumpik Deldkur — filed from feyward_dark_rooms_and_balcony_planning. Mechanics as the table rules them; the archive records custody.

waluipedia.note: pocketed like a receipt; read in full by Waluigi

description.value:
A card to Woodfellow’s library in the Feyward manor, given to Hjumpik by the goblin patron Artameer Fellow during the Revel crisis (~18 Harvestide, 1040 BF). Woodfellow issues cards only to people he assesses as genuinely knowledgeable; the return policy is one week, or the borrower becomes a book.

  • Access to Woodfellow’s library and its rare fey texts.
  • One week to return a book, or the borrower becomes a book. Woodfellow is equanimous about this.
  • Issued on an assessment of knowledge — a credential with actual standards, which Waluigi notes was not extended to Waluigi.

Obtained: Given to Hjumpik in the library after he found ‘Concerning the Nature and Sustenance of Revels Eternal’; Artameer Fellow is the patron whose previous card Wario stole to check out the Feyward Book of Many Things.

On the record: received from Artameer Fellow; nothing borrowed on it yet.

The transformation-as-late-fee system is the most effective library enforcement mechanism Waluigi has encountered in any documented plane. — W.

description.value:
The wolf-pelt onesie Hjumpik has worn for three Feyward sessions. The Colour Division identified him by it from a doorway — not by description, sigil or writ — and his defence that all dwarves use wolf pelt did not land.

  • Signature garment: ‘Hey — you ARE Hjumpik. You have the signature wolf-pelt onesie on.’
  • Warm, which matters in a manor that keeps rearranging its weather.
  • Evidence, as of 2 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock). Waluigi had never once thought of it as evidence.

Obtained: Worn. The record does not say where it came from; it says who recognised it.

On the record: worn — and now the thing the Legion looks for.

Four special forces operatives crossed a planar boundary into a house full of carnivorous architecture to collect one contractor, and the identification was made on a garment. — W.
